validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE checks all pass. REX is unambiguously real and well documented: FERC-certificated interstate transmission pipeline, PHMSA-regulated (PHMSA enforcement docket 2022-0044 names 'Rockies Express Pipeline, LLC' as a Tallgrass subsidiary and describes 42-inch pipe at Class 1/Class 2 locations), covered continuously in SEC filings 2005-2024 and trade press. Correctly classified as a natural gas transmission trunk (not gathering/distribution) -- confirmed by the SEC 2017 exhibit's own description ('approximately 1,712-mile natural gas transmission pipeline') and by PHMSA's Part 192 transmission-pipeline enforcement framework applied to it. Not a duplicate: checked against the roster -- P2517 'Rockies Express Gas Pipeline' (len=0, cap=1000 MMcf/d, Illinois) is the Cheyenne Hub Enhancement compression-only project on the SAME system, correctly a separate row (a capacity-enhancement scope with no new mainline pipe, per the standing expansion-with-no-new-pipe convention -- its len=0 is correct, do not 'fix'). No other roster row plausibly duplicates this Main Line segment. Opened/read: hydrocarbons-technology/offshore-technology redirect page, Wikipedia, SEC 424B5 (2008), SEC 8-K exhibit (2017 Ultra Resources settlement), PHMSA NOPV enforcement letter (2022, read via pdftotext after WebFetch/curl 403s), EIA todayinenergy article, 4 of this row's ~30 harvested wiki citations opened directly (hydrocarbons-technology, SEC exhibit 9911172017, EIA data page, ogj.com 2009 final-leg article); several more (IJGlobal, downstreamtoday.com pieces, rigzone 2006/2008 pieces, criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com, oilandgaswatch.org) were not opened this pass -- most are pre-2010 construction-phase news that would only corroborate already-settled facts (in-service dates), not the live attribute/spec questions below.

validity.recommendation: update Owner1/Owner1% to Tallgrass Energy 100%; remove Phillips 66 as an owner -- it sold its 25% stake
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet reads Owner1=Tallgrass Energy [75%], Owner2=Phillips 66 [25%] -- this is the CORRECT pre-2024 structure (confirmed by the row's own harvested citations: businesswire.com 2016-03-29 'Tallgrass Development Announces Agreement to Acquire Additional Interest' and hartenergy.com 2016-03-31 both describe Tallgrass building up to that split) but it is now stale. On 2024-06-14 Tallgrass Energy, LP (via a subsidiary) acquired Phillips 66's remaining 25% non-operated common equity interest in Rockies Express Pipeline LLC for an enterprise value of ~$1.275 billion ($685M pre-tax cash to Phillips 66); Tallgrass now owns 100%. Confirmed independently by Oil & Gas Journal ('Tallgrass Energy to gain full ownership of REX in deal with Phillips 66') and Rigzone ('Phillips 66 Sells Stake In REX Pipeline To Tallgrass') -- two separate trade-press origins reporting the same company disclosure, plus NS Energy Business as a third. Phillips 66's own investor-relations press release states the same figures but 403'd on every fetch attempt (WebFetch and curl, both with browser UA) and Wayback was rate-limited (429) throughout this session, so it is not in proposed_refs -- OGJ + Rigzone stand on their own as 2 independent sources. Operator is unaffected (Tallgrass subsidiary already operates REX and continues to). No percentage for a residual Phillips 66 stake was reported anywhere -- the deal was 100% of the remaining interest.

validity.recommendation: re-verify LengthKnown against the pipeline's current stated mileage; 1685 mi does not match the current owner's own 2024 figure of 1,714 mi (nor any of the several other mileages the system has carried over time)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=1685 mi. REX's stated length has genuinely changed over time as laterals/receipt points were added (this is a real length-genealogy issue, not just noisy reporting): ~1,323 mi at the original 2005-2006 open-season stage (naturalgasintel.com, 2006-03-01, describing only the then-firm-committed mainline); 1,663 mi at the 2005 FERC-filing stage (naturalgasintel search results); 1,679 mi widely cited for the completed 2009 system (Wikipedia infobox; the row's own cited hydrocarbons-technology/offshore-technology page after its 2026 redirect; SEC KMP 424B5 2008 prospectus supplement, sec.gov, verified, describes REX as 'extending from Opal, Wyoming and Meeker, Colorado to Clarington, Ohio' at that stage); 1,712 mi in a Tallgrass SEC 8-K exhibit filed 2017-01-17 (sec.gov, verified); and 1,714 mi in the CURRENT (2024) disclosure -- Phillips 66's own divestiture announcement describes REX as a '1,714-mile pipeline system,' independently confirmed word-for-word by both Oil & Gas Journal and Rigzone (both verified, both name the pipeline). None of these five figures is 1685. The 1,714 figure is both the most recent and the most authoritative (stated by the pipeline's own owner in its own 2024 SEC-adjacent disclosure), so it is the best current value, but flagging as a concern rather than a clean fill because GEM's own convention for which vintage of a growing system to record is not something I can adjudicate alone -- Baird should confirm whether 1685 was ever a real intermediate figure or is simply a transcription of one of the other numbers.

validity.recommendation: re-verify Capacity; 4050 MMcf/d does not match any capacity figure found in current sourcing, and the pipeline's true 'capacity' is not a single number (it differs by direction and has grown through several enhancement projects)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=4050 MMcf/d. I could not find ANY source stating 4050/4,050 MMcf/d for REX, and REX's capacity is not well represented by one number: original west-to-east design capacity was 1.8 Bcf/d (SEC 424B5 2008, verified; Rigzone 2024 article, verified, states the same 'design capacity' figure); the Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project raised EAST-TO-WEST capacity in Zone 3 specifically to 2.6 Bcf/d (SEC 8-K exhibit 2017, verified; EIA todayinenergy article, verified, describes the buildout toward that figure in increments); and as of the 2024 ownership sale, Phillips 66/OGJ/Rigzone (all verified) describe REX as providing 'over 5 Bcf/d of bi-directional' service -- i.e. the two directions summed, not a single nameplate figure. 1.8+2.6=4.4 Bcf/d, still not 4.05, and 'over 5 Bcf/d bidirectional' is a different kind of figure (combined throughput capability, not unidirectional design capacity) from what GEM's single Capacity field implies. Left the candidate value blank rather than guess which of these numbers GEM intends; recommend Baird decide whether Capacity should record the original 1.8 Bcf/d west-to-east design capacity (1800 MMcf/d), the current >5000 MMcf/d bidirectional figure, or something else, then re-source accordingly.

Did not have time this pass to pull the SEC 10-K balance-sheet note for Rockies Express Pipeline LLC's capitalized construction cost, which is the source most likely to state an exact figure -- worth a follow-up.

Searched extensively but found no single, unambiguous 'proposed' date -- candidates conflict depending on milestone: a PitchBook company-profile summary gives 2004 as REX's founding year; Kinder Morgan/Sempra's FERC pre-filing request was granted in November 2005; naturalgasintel.com (2006-03-01, verified) covers securing FULL firm-transportation commitments for the (then) 1,323-mile/$4bn project, implying the actual open season/announcement preceded that by months; and one search summary (unverified, could not locate the underlying primary article) claimed 'first announced in August 2005.' Rather than pick one, left blank -- recommend a follow-up pass specifically to pin down FERC's pre-filing docket date or the original Kinder Morgan/Sempra open-season press release, neither of which I could isolate with confidence in the time available.

REX was built in three distinct phases over 2005-2009 (Entrega/Zone 1 authorized Aug 2005, in service Feb 2006; REX-West/Zone 2 in service Dec 2007-May 2008; REX-East/Zone 3 FERC-approved May 2008, in service Nov 2009), and I could not find a single primary source stating one clean 'construction start' year for the system as a whole without conflating phases -- search results returned contradictory framings (one summary said construction 'did not begin until 2007-2008' while the Entrega segment was demonstrably already operating by Feb 2006, which is impossible unless its construction began materially earlier, in 2005). Left blank rather than force a year; the earliest defensible candidate is 2005 (Entrega construction, to support the Feb 2006 in-service date) but I could not source that specific claim to my own satisfaction this pass.

Also tried the companion PHMSA Special Permit Alternative MAOP document (PHMSA-2022-0044-...-SPAF.pdf) which would likely state the same figure from a second discrete federal filing, but it 403'd on every fetch attempt (WebFetch, curl with browser UA) and Wayback was rate-limited (429) throughout the session -- worth a follow-up to reach a second source.

Per gem_schema.md, FuelSource wants a single named upstream field/plant/facility, not a basin or a generic 'natural gas' restatement. REX does not have one: it is a long-haul trunk line that aggregates gas from multiple producing basins via numerous interconnects -- the Piceance and Uinta basins (western Colorado/eastern Utah) and the Green River basin (via a long-term capacity lease on the Overthrust Pipeline near Opal, WY), received through interconnections with Colorado Interstate Gas, Wyoming Interstate Pipeline, and others (per naturalgasintel.com/EIA sourcing above). There is no single named field or plant that would be an honest FuelSource value for this row; forcing one of the basin names in would misrepresent a multi-basin trunk as a single-source gathering line. Left blank per the schema's own instruction ('if you can't attribute one, leave it blank and note why -- do not default it').
